anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Address to Ambrosius and Tatiana; Phil 3:13 motto reprised.
Promise of greater treatment; indulgence asked. T ends fol. 38v.

choices.why: diathleō = contend through; the treatise was an athletic contest to the end — agon frame closed.

pass_a_gloss: Closing: the prayer-problem 'contested' to the author's power for Ambrose and Tatiana; hope of diviner treatment as they press forward and pray for him; indulgence for the present.
pass_b_english: This, to my power, I contested for the problem of prayer, and for the prayer in the Gospels, and the words before it with Matthew — most studious and most genuine brothers in godliness, Ambrosius and Tatiana. I despair not — with your 'things before' stretched toward and your 'things behind' forgotten, and your being in these things praying for us — of holding more and diviner things in all these from the giving God, and, receiving again, discussing the same things more greatly grown and loftier and plainer. Only, at present, with indulgence, shall you meet with these (Philippians 3:13).
